page: Amazon Web Services i2.2xlarge is a legacy generation, storage-optimized virtual machine running on the Xen hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 25 MB of L3 cache, along with 61.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.62 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX and AES-NI, but lack modern instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX, or SHA-NI. The instance contains 1600 GB of attached local solid-state storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps, with zero integrated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the older nature of the underlying hardware. PassMark CPU testing shows average multi-core throughput at 8,839.65 points, and stress-ng performance registers within the middle tier for both single-threaded (1,619.98) and multi-threaded (7,138.99) execution. However, single-core efficiency lags significantly in newer workloads, as reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 529.0 and multi-core score of 2,015.0, both landing in the bottom tier. In-memory operations display varying results: large block uncached read bandwidth reaches 40.1 GB/sec, while cached read and write throughput remain in lower performance quartiles. Database operations in PassMark achieve an average score of 3,356.02, whereas Redis SET benchmarks reach 3.05 million operations per second.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the i2.2xlarge lies in its pairing of large local SSD space and generous memory capacity against older CPU execution capabilities. For applications that require high local storage capacity and substantial RAM buffers without intensive per-core computational demands, it maintains utility. The instance is suited for intermediate database servers, NoSQL datastores, caching tiers, log indexers, and transactional processing workloads that rely heavily on local disk capacity rather than cutting-edge instruction pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i2.2xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores. It features 61.0 GB of RAM, a baseline 1 Gbps network connection, and 1600 GB of local SSD storage, with no graphics hardware included. CPU and memory benchmarks show intermediate performance in multi-threaded computational workloads such as stress-ng and PassMark, alongside solid database operational metrics. However, single-core processing and newer vector tasks are constrained by older Ivy Bridge architecture without AVX-512 extensions. The server is well positioned for memory-heavy and disk-intensive deployments, including relational databases, NoSQL clusters, caching layers, and transactional backend processing where substantial local disk space and high memory density are the primary operational requirements.
